title: Asking About a Flat to Rent

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Good morning, Harbour Lettings. Megan speaking. How can I help you?

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Hello. My name is Daniel Price. I saw your advert for a one-bedroom flat near the park, and I'd like to ask about it.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Yes, of course. That flat is on Garden Road. It's on the second floor, and it has a lovely view of the park.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Great. How much is the rent?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: It's seven hundred pounds a month, and that includes water. You pay for the electricity yourself.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Okay, that's fine. Is the flat furnished?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Yes, it is. There's a bed, a sofa and a small table in the kitchen, but there isn't a washing machine.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: That's all right. Can I see the flat this week?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Yes. Are you free on Thursday? We could meet at half past four.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Thursday is good, but I finish work at five. Could we meet a bit later?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Let me check. Well, the owner is busy after five, but he could come at ten to five, if you can leave work early.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Hmm, I think I can do that. I'll ask my manager. If not, I'll call you back.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: No problem. Now, is there anything else you would like to know?

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Yes. I don't have a car, so how do I get there from the city centre? Is there a bus?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Number twelve bus stops outside the building, and it takes fifteen minutes to the centre. There's also a small supermarket on the corner.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: That sounds perfect. And what about pets? I have a small cat.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: I'm afraid the owner doesn't allow animals in the flat. He had a problem with the carpet last year. But he might think about it if you pay a bigger deposit.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: I see. A bigger deposit is a possibility, but I'd need to think it over. How much is the normal deposit?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: It's one month's rent, so seven hundred pounds. Please bring your passport and a letter from your employer when you come on Thursday.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Okay, I will. Thanks for your help, Megan. It sounds like a nice place, so I'm quite hopeful, though the cat might be a problem.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Don't worry, Daniel. We'll talk about it on Thursday. Goodbye!

items.explanation: Half past four is too early for Daniel, so the owner offers ten to five.

items.explanation: The number twelve bus stops outside the building and goes to the centre.

options.text: Pets are fine with a letter.

items.explanation: The owner does not allow animals in the flat, even small ones.

items.explanation: The carpet was the owner's earlier problem, but he might change his mind if Daniel pays a bigger deposit.
